front.title: Machine-Adversary Resistance (MARS): A Rating Framework for System Resistance to Autonomous AI Adversaries

abstract.t: Existing AI-security frameworks catalogue the threats an organisation faces and the controls it ought to implement. They answer the question "what should I do?". They do not answer the question that now decides survival: "if an autonomous AI adversary attacks this system, does it hold, and how well?". This document defines Machine- Adversary Resistance (MARS), an outcome rating that measures how well a tool, system, or defended surface resists an autonomous AI adversary. MARS scores a target on five resistance axes, assigns a zero-to-five rating gated by the weakest axis, and requires that any rating above two be backed by measured, tamper-evident evidence rather than self-declaration. MARS is an outcome layer intended to sit above, and to consume, existing control catalogues; it is not a replacement for them. This document is a proposal and a starting point for discussion, not a ratified standard.
